answer: A probationary reward ramp raises sybil costs. A new identity keeps only 10 percent of its reward for six epochs, and the other 90 percent sits in escrow, released only if its graded answers across all six epochs average 2 or better. The climb moves at glacier pace because each epoch must be earned with graded work. A farm of 1,000 fake identities must fund 6,000 graded epochs at a tenth of normal pay, and one failed epoch burns that identity's escrow. A throwaway account is cheap, like a jetty, but it cannot dock at full pay until six epochs are done, and the work costs more than saffron.
